title: No chain-check endpoint exists in the ownership map, the API specification or the technical specification of rwb-access
source: Context pack P4 (the four provided REST operations of rwb-access: GET /admin/access-log, GET /admin/roles, GET /me/session, POST /admin/break-glass-grants; the five tables; JOB-18; events none); Ownership Map v1 and TSD P4 v3 Appendix T-A.1 (API-P4-004 to API-P4-021, none of them a chain check); FSD P4 v3 A2.26 (a feature with an intent, steps, roles and acceptance criteria but no interface section and no endpoint); legacy story RWB-E8-015 (its Endpoints table names the rule-version paths, not a chain check); Work Package B2-P4-015 (acs AC1 and AC2, patterns DP03, DP06, DP13 and DP19, and no path)
section: Section 12.1 of both slices (the two provided operations) and section 3 and 11 of RWB-P4-E8015-APP (the paths and the run-row fields)
description: The legacy feature FEAT-ADM-10 is a chain check with no interface of its own in any source: the FSD gives it a system trigger and a result written to the decision log, the TSD gives it no component and no endpoint, and the ownership map gives rwb-access four REST operations, none of which runs or reports a chain check. The two paths the app and the contract slices need are therefore fixed on the DP-13 base as POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/chain-checks (the run, no body, Idempotency-Key) and GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/chain-checks (the report, with the outcome filter and paging), and the run-row field names, the outcome value set, the checkpoint element and the report page are fixed by the contract of RWB-P4-E8015-CON. The two slices state the placeholder next to every such field and cite this row, and the fragment and the story files carry the same citation set. The value is not invented: the paths are a naming decision on the service base, the fields are the minimum a reader of the check needs, and both are subject to the contract review and to the ownership map at D1.
evidence: Context pack P4 headed 'REST operations provided (4)' lists GET /admin/access-log, GET /admin/roles, GET /me/session and POST /admin/break-glass-grants and no chain check; TSD P4 v3 Appendix T-A.1 lists API-P4-004 to API-P4-021 with no chain check; FSD P4 v3 A2.26 carries sections A2.26.1 to A2.26.4 with no interface table; the legacy RWB-E8-015 Endpoints table names POST /admin/rule-versions and its approve path; the two delivered story files cite CG-B2-P4-015-1 in section 1, section 3 and section 12.1 of the contract slice and in section 12.1 of the app slice
owner_role: Solution architect with the rwb-access tech lead
proposed: Register the two operations in the Ownership Map v1 and in the API Specification as API-P4-022 (POST /admin/chain-checks) and API-P4-023 (GET /admin/chain-checks) under the rwb-access base, and add the chain check to the TSD P4 endpoint inventory. If the ownership map must stay as it is, state that the capability is served by these two paths and that no other story owns them. At D1 the row is numbered once and every placeholder inside the two story files and the two fragments is rewritten to the numbered id.

title: The record code, the chain order and batch of the walk, the Schedule start time and the same-day channel to Compliance are not specified for the daily chain check
source: Program BRD v4 REQ-DRI-003 and NFR-035 (the chain is checked every day and a break is reported to Compliance the same day, with no time of day, no window, no batch size and no channel); FSD P4 v3 A2.26.2 (three generic steps: a trigger, the feature, the result written to the decision log); TSD P4 v3 T6.3 (the audit rows of a rule package change only); Architecture v5 slides 20, 28 and 44 and Decision Log v10 ADR-022 (local decision record plus central ledger, no code set and no order for a local chain); legacy story RWB-E8-015 (AC1 says 'with the rule version' and names no code, no order and no channel)
section: Section 11 of both slices (the entry, the order of the walk and the channel) and section 12.3 of RWB-P4-E8015-APP (the payload of the record message)
description: The daily cadence and the same-day obligation are fixed by REQ-DRI-003 and NFR-035, and the story records the run under both. What the sources do not fix is the rest of the run: the record code the library gives a chain check, the order in which a local chain is walked and the batch size of the walk, the start time of the Schedule, the parameter row that holds the window, and the channel by which a break reaches the Compliance and PDPA officer role on the same day. Each of these is written in the two story files as the placeholder that cites this row, and each is carried by an assumption: the record code comes from the library's code set, the order and batch are parameter rows read through DP-06, the start time is a parameter row, and the same-day report is the breach row plus the report read, with a notice through rwb-comms left out of this work package because it is not in the dependency lists. No value is invented and no interval is written in code.
evidence: Program BRD v4 rows REQ-DRI-003 and NFR-035 carry the cadence and the same-day report and no time, no window, no batch and no channel; FSD P4 v3 A2.26.2 step 1 names the trigger in the general form 'a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer'; TSD P4 v3 T6.3 names the change checklist and the checksum of a rule package version only; the two story files carry the placeholder in section 11 and in section 12.3 of the app slice with the citation CG-B2-P4-015-2; ASM-B2-P4-015-4 records the applied defaults
owner_role: Solution architect with the Compliance and PDPA officer
proposed: Fix the four values at the contract review of RWB-P4-E8015-CON: the library's record code for a chain check, the chain order and the batch size as parameter rows, the start time of chain-check-daily as a parameter row, and the same-day channel to Compliance. If a notice channel is required, add the rwb-comms contract dependency to the dependency map of the story set and a C row to the app slice rather than a hidden call.

title: The legacy RWB-E8-015 endpoints, data table and permission checks belong to other stories and another service, and the FSD grants the feature no user action
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md RWB-E8-015 (Endpoints POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/rule-versions Rules and parameters C and its approve path Rules and parameters A; Data decision_log_entry, rule_row and role; Permission checks Rules and parameters C for RW-COE and A for RW-RISK; Screens SCR-39 and SCR-41); FSD P4 v3 A2.26.3.3 (None; runs unattended | Internal audit also uses); TSD P4 v3 T6.1 (RW-AUDIT holds R in Rules and parameters, Reference data and Platform administration and no C and no A anywhere); TSD P4 v3 T6.3 and Appendix T-A (the rule-version paths are API-P4-015 to API-P4-019 of the rule package journey)
section: Section 1, 3, 10 and 15 of RWB-P4-E8015-APP (the endpoints, the data and the rights of the legacy story)
description: The legacy story carries the generic administration template: two rule-version endpoints, the three tables of the administration module, Rules and parameters C and A for two roles, and the two rule and limit screens. None of it describes a chain check. The capability is unattended per the FSD role table, the only right that fits a read-only walk with an on-demand run is Platform administration R, which RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY, RW-PLATADM, RW-SECADM, RW-DATASTEW and RW-COE hold, and the tables of the legacy data block are P7's (decision_log_entry, rule_row) and this service's own read side (role). The two story files therefore implement no legacy endpoint and no legacy table, keep the legacy intent and the two legacy criteria, and record the mismatch here instead of copying it forward. The legacy screens SCR-39 and SCR-41 are stated as not part of the feature, and the report is placed on SCR-43 Roles and access, which the FSD describes as the roles, permissions, scope, group mapping and access log screen.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E8-015 Endpoints, Data, Screen and states and Permission checks tables as quoted in the source column; FSD P4 v3 A2.26.3.3; TSD P4 v3 T6.1 letters for RW-AUDIT, RW-COE and RW-RISK; TSD P4 v3 Appendix T-A.1 operation names; the app slice cites CG-B2-P4-015-3 in section 1, section 3 and section 15 and the contract slice in section 12.1 and section 15
owner_role: Business analyst with the solution architect
proposed: Correct the legacy story at the next master version: replace the rule-version endpoints with the chain-check paths or state that the legacy block was inherited from the administration template, replace the Rules and parameters C and A checks with Platform administration R, and replace the data block with the decision-record entry. No change is made to the legacy master in this run.

title: The daily chain check has no job row in the Batch and Scheduling Design and the workflow kit dependency is absent from the Work Package
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Microservice Architecture v5.md and Recovery Workbench Batch and Scheduling Design v4.md (the job table names JOB-18 Access review list, six-monthly, rwb-access, and no chain check); Program BRD v4 NFR-035 and REQ-DRI-003 (a daily check); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-10 (Quartz, JOB-nn, replaced by a Temporal Schedule through the workflow kit, H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON); Work Package B2-P4-015 (H: RWB-P4-E8015-CON, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-N001-CON; patterns DP03, DP06, DP13, DP19)
section: Section 3, 12.5 and 12.6 of RWB-P4-E8015-APP (the workflow, the Schedule and the missing dependency) and section 13 of both slices
description: The feature runs unattended on a daily trigger and the target replaces the Quartz job with a Temporal Schedule on the owner's queue, so the story declares the Schedule chain-check-daily on the queue rwb-access and the workflow AccessChainCheckWorkflow with three activities. Two things are missing around it. The job table of Architecture v5 and of the Batch and Scheduling Design carries JOB-18 (access review list, six-monthly) and no row for a daily chain check, so the run has no job identifier. And the platform story that publishes the workflow kit and the Schedule API (RWB-PLT-E1071-CON) is not in this Work Package's H list, although the Schedule cannot be built without it, so the metadata is kept exactly as the Work Package fixes it and the missing H is stated in the story and in section 13 instead. DP-10 is not claimed in Patterns applied because the legacy key carries no Quartz marker.
evidence: Architecture v5 job table row 'JOB-18 | Access review list | six-monthly | rwb-access | Schedule' and the same row in Batch and Scheduling Design v4 with no chain-check row; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-10 dependency column 'H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON'; Work Package B2-P4-015 H list as quoted; the app slice cites CG-B2-P4-015-4 in section 1, section 3 and section 13; ASM-B2-P4-015-7 records the prerequisite
owner_role: Solution architect with the platform workflow owner
proposed: Add the daily chain check of rwb-access to the job table with its own JOB-nn row, and add RWB-PLT-E1071-CON to the H list of RWB-P4-E8015-APP in the dependency map and in the plan, so that the Schedule has a declared prerequisite. If the check stays outside the job table, state in the Batch and Scheduling Design that each service verifies its own decision-record chain daily and that only P7 holds the central row.
